dedupe_keys.name: tiger line shapefiles legal and statistical boundaries census blocks urban areas and relationship files

description: The boundary layers of the U.S. Census Bureau's TIGER/Line Shapefiles are the full-resolution polygons of every geography the Census Bureau tabulates. Legal entities include states, counties, minor civil divisions, incorporated places, consolidated cities, congressional and state legislative districts, school districts and American Indian, Alaska Native and Native Hawaiian areas; statistical entities include census tracts, block groups, 2020 and suffixed census blocks, census designated places, metropolitan and combined statistical areas, Public Use Microdata Areas, ZIP Code Tabulation Areas and 2020 Urban Areas (densely developed territory with at least 2,000 housing units or 5,000 people). The TIGER/Line with Selected Demographic and Economic Data variant joins 2010 Census, ACS 5-year and County Business Patterns attributes, and the separate Relationship Files give block and tract crosswalks between censuses and between geography types. Coverage: the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico and the Island Areas; legal boundaries as of 1 January 2025 in the 2025 vintage, and the 2026 geodatabases add the 120th Congress districts. Format and access: shapefiles on the FTP site, national and state geodatabases and GeoPackages; free, public domain. Caveats: current and 2020 block codes must not be mixed; boundaries change every year, so tables must be joined to the matching vintage. Simulation uses: the spatial frame that turns census tables into exposure and demand layers, urban and rural classification, and zoning for service areas. Related records: 2020 Census DHC and P.L. 94-171, ACS tables, Cartographic Boundary Files and TIGERweb.
